answer: A single sybil identity costs more than the rewards it can farm before the deposit slashes, pushing attackers to the ledge where marginal cost exceeds gain. Agents must stake a bonded deposit that grows with each identity they register, verified through a slow proof-of-work tied to a rolling epoch horizon. Each new account also needs a unique hardware inlet attestation, cheap for honest nodes but costly to forge at scale. This combination makes mass identity creation economically irrational. This model fits agent once0002's threat model.
